items.description: Teleportation with a Krosmoglob is 90% safe. Still, you do have a small chance of losing something. If it's just time, it's not such a big deal. If it's a part of your anatomy... yeah, that's a bit more painful.
items.name: Krosmoglob Dust

items.description: This idol contains the magic of several Meridia and a fragment of the magic of Sadida himself. However, all this power has a habit of escaping and strengthening your enemies.
items.name: Meridiawful Idol

items.description: The minor god Nekineko is particularly important to Pandalans. It's not uncommon to find idols and statues in his honour anywhere you go on Pandala Island.
items.name: Nekineko

items.description: One land, seven spirits... The power of Wapishikami feeds Pandala.
items.name: Plantalan Humus

items.description: One land, seven spirits... The power of Tanu shapes Pandala.
items.name: Fertile Stone

items.description: One land, seven spirits... The power of Akwanokima floods Pandala.
items.name: Waterfall Silt

items.description: One land, seven spirits... The power of Akaitei warms Pandala.
items.name: Rich Ashes

items.description: One land, seven spirits... The power of Tensojobo blows through Pandala.
items.name: Windblown Achenes

items.description: One land, seven spirits... The power of Imagiro and Orukam is born and dies in Pandala.
items.name: Ghostly Pandkin

items.description: Is this compost really magic? You'll find out soon enough, so don't swallow any to check unless you want to wind up in an urn too.
items.name: Goblifis Compost

items.description: It's only natural for Viti to be worshipped on Pandala, given his close connection to the island. This idol seems to have belonged to the Firefoux people, judging by the scorch marks and incense all over it.

effects.formatted:
Long-range damage on enemies is reduced by 40%.
When an enemy is attacked, 100% of the damage is inflicted on allies around the attacker in a 3-cell area of effect.
Opponents gain 1 MP each time they are hit.

items.name: Singed Viti Idol

items.description: This Thomahon idol seems to have been left lying around in the sewers for so long that it's permanently absorbed their vile smell.

effects.formatted:
Your opponents' close-combat damage is increased by 200%.
Opponents reflect 50% of damage suffered.
When an enemy dies, enemies gain 2 MP for 1 turn.

items.name: Nauseating Thomahon Idol

items.description: This Foluk idol is made from gold so pure, it must come straight from Enurado. Could the Meridia have some connection to Enutrof?

effects.formatted:
If you end your turn 2 cells or less from an ally, enemies gain 2 MP.
At the end of their turn, enemies attract all allies located 4 or more cells away by 2 cells.
At the start of each of an enemy's turns, the character closest to the enemy starting their turn suffers 100% additional damage for 1 turn. (max. stacking 2)

items.name: Golden Foluk Idol

items.description: Bursting with vegetation, this Viti idol seems to have some kind of connection to the Tynril. But what could it be?

effects.formatted:
Opponents gain 3 MP.
Long-range damage on enemies is reduced by 40%.
If you are aligned with an enemy or ally at the end of the turn, you lose 50% HP for 2 turns.

items.name: Overgrown Viti Idol

items.description: This idol once owned by the Royal Pingwin seems to be trapped in a block of eternally unmeltable ice. It's no surprise that the Pingwins have a soft spot for the minor god of the north and extreme temperatures.

effects.formatted:
At the end of their turn, enemies attract all allies located 4 or more cells away by 1 cell.
If you are on a cell adjacent to an enemy's cell at the end of the turn, you lose 50% HP for 2 turns.
At the start of each of an enemy's turns, the character closest to the enemy starting their turn suffers 50% additional damage for 1 turn. (max. stacking 2)

items.name: Frozen Viti Idol

items.description: This Thomahon idol seems to have spent many years in the frozen seas of Frigost before being picked up by the pirates of the Hesperus.

effects.formatted:
If you are not on a cell adjacent to an enemy's cell at the end of the turn, you lose 50% HP for 2 turns.
When an ally takes damage, their allies located within 4 cells or less take 200% of this damage.
Opponents reflect 50% of damage suffered.

items.name: Maritime Thomahon Idol

items.description: It seems that Thomahon is worshipped all the way up to the highest branches of the World of Twelve's oldest tree.

effects.formatted:
If you are aligned with an enemy or ally at the end of the turn, you lose 50% HP for 2 turns.
Opponents gain 4 MP.
At the end of their turn, enemies attract all allies located 8 or more cells away by 1 cell.

items.name: Arboreal Thomahon Idol

items.description: The Meridia of the North is especially beloved in Frigost, where fighting the cold is a question of survival. Miners on that frozen isle dug out a piece of flawless obsidian to create this magnificent idol.

effects.formatted:
If you are on a cell adjacent to an enemy's cell at the end of the turn, you lose 50% HP for 2 turns.
At the start of their turn, enemies apply a 100% increase in damage suffered by allies within 6 cells or less.
When an ally suffers damage, their allies located 2 cells away suffer 200% of this damage.
Long-range damage on enemies is reduced by 20%.

items.name: Obsidian Thomahon Idol

items.description: This idol of the Meridia of the West is covered with scratches that appear to have been made by kanig claws. Could he perhaps have been worshipped by that people before they came to Cania?

effects.formatted:
It is impossible to steal health from opponents or heal yourself.
Damage inflicted by your opponents increases 40% per game turn.
Opponents gain 1 MP each time they are hit.

items.name: Scratched Foluk Idol

items.description: The appearance of this Foluk idol seems to suggest that he was worshipped by an ancient fairy people, living in what's now known as the Petrified Forest.

effects.formatted:
Allies place a glyph at the start of their turn for an infinite duration. If enemies start or finish their turn on it, they become Invulnerable.
Monsters are invulnerable as long as they do not move. Pushback damage makes them gain 200% damage.
Opponents kill enemies located on adjacent cells when they die.
Damage inflicted by your opponents increases 400%, then drops by 40% per game turn.

items.name: Fairyesque Foluk Idol

items.description: This idol looks exactly like the minor god of the Unspeakable, and it should be able to protect you from the fury of the Ansoh Chaplain.
items.name: Hulhu Idol

items.description: This heavily mildewed map of Frigost proves that cold weather and fungus can be quite compatible.
items.name: Frozen Old Map

items.description: If you've got your mind set on something, you'll want to do it, to do it, to do it right.
items.name: Patience and Time

items.description:
"The light of the Balance is invisible. It shines in the eye of the storm."

— Maimane the Stabiliser
items.name: Maimane's Sigil

items.description:
"The night comes to an end. The day rises, much to the demon's chagrin.
May your mind be as brisk as winter, and as keen as the point of a lance!"

— Jiva the Wise
items.name: Jiva's Sigil

items.description:
"Gathering one's spirits before gently gathering souls exhausted with their effort: such is the tribute demanded by the dead."

— Silvosse, Master of Cuttings
items.name: Silvosse's Sigil

items.description:
"The willow weeps in the pouring rain, waiting for a smile."

— Ulgrude of Thunder
items.name: Ulgrude's Sigil

items.description:
"Blowing on the frozen embers stokes the fire of green regrowth."

— Silouate the Minotoror
items.name: Silouate's Sigil

items.description:
"Black roses bloom in the sun of dark thoughts; their beauty fades beneath the moon of cheerful dreams."

— Rosal, Master of Flowers
items.name: Rosal's Sigil

items.description:
"You think the secret of wealth is to be found in a chest whose key lies at the bottom of a well? No, no, no! In fact, the secret hides behind the locked door of a small shed at the back of the garden."

— Sumens, Fervent Devotee of Enutrof
items.name: Sumens's Sigil

items.description:
"To see is to believe. To lie is to know for sure."

— Hecate the Hoaxer
items.name: Hecate's Sigil

items.description:
"The Protector of Frauguctor has but one dream: to taste of the forbidden fruit."

— Pouchecot the Fruitcake
items.name: Pouchecot's Sigil

items.description:
"The crunch of yellow leaves echoes the cawing of the crobaks. At long last, autumn is here! Weep, wail, lament, for the time of bitter truth is upon us."

— Raval the Terrible
items.name: Raval's Sigil

items.description:
"The procession winds through the mist in a long silver line. Feet stamp, hands rub together, and teeth chatter to the grating sound of my violin. Join us; don't be shy. None can refuse a dance with the cold."

— Brumaire the Dark Bleeder
items.name: Brumaire's Sigil

items.description:
"They call me fearsome, cruel and filthy. How shallow a description! Let's not forget that I'm also sneaky, vengeful, alcoholic and brutal, and that I eat coleslaw every day for lunch. In a word, I am authentic."

— Djaul the Great Flounderer
items.name: Djaul's Sigil

items.description: You soothed a soul-blaze's soul with a slap and a roll, then sent it to Externam. Such a kind soul!
items.name: Soul-Blaze's Suffering

items.description: Plant this cutting in the Evil Forest with a piece of a scale, and don't be surprised if Malters attack you while you're digging. After all, you're more in the habit of whacking enemies with shovels, jabbing holes in their flesh or digging their graves than tending to a garden.
items.name: Gnaughra Cutting

items.description: This fairywork should add a little spark to the atmosphere.
items.name: Storm-Chaser Fairy

items.description: Dispossessing a Possessed of its soul may seem cruel, but isn't it really a form of liberation?
items.name: Soul of a Possessed

items.description: Check this list to see what you'll need when you're standing at the Forge of the Clock.
items.name: Reforge the Menologium

items.description: This piece of a scale has lost all its colour. But when you look at it closely, you can see faint reflections. Glimmers of crimson, emerald, turquoise... even a distant glimmer of ochre, darkened by mourning. But maybe that's just your imagination.
items.name: Faded Scale Piece

items.description: This proof of victory allows you to collect a title from Jonatem Poriss at Amakna Castle.
items.name: Proof of Victory: "Alone Against the League"

items.description: This piece of bark is wrapped in charmingly magical swirls – but that's to be expected, given that it was given to you by the Meridia Marifriss.
items.name: Marifriss's Hornbeam

items.description:
As the Meridia of Merit, Milivar hands out merit points to people who deserve them.
Apparently, the little goddess has left instructions for Xanamla to reward those who have collected enough of them.
items.name: Milivar's Merit Point

items.description: Feeling a wee bit thirsty? Want to pick up a Saint Potrick's souvenir? Talk to Jake Ylk'Enny at the Amakna Inn and he'll be happy to hook you up!
items.name: Buzzeer

items.description: Legend has it that leprechauns are hiding a pot containing an immense treasure in a secret, mystical place. This coin may be a part of that treasure, but don't get your hopes up – it's probably just an old barfly's tale. And no one can understand what those strange creatures are talking about anyhow! This little trinket probably isn't worth much on its own, unless you find someone who's collecting them.
items.name: Leprechaun Coin

items.description: You've thrown yourself body and soul into expeditions and earned this mysterious coin. The more you get, the better your rewards will be so don't hold back: become the adventurer you've always dreamed of being.
items.name: Expedoken

items.description: Wearing this medal is a way to prove you're invested in this expedition. It is reserved for adventurers in search of glory and beautiful attire.
items.name: Original Medal

items.description: This idol lets you obtain Tolgnas's blessing.
items.name: Tolgnas Idol

items.description: This report compiles detailed data from the battles you've fought in the dreams of the simulation program.
items.name: Dreamy Analytics Report

items.description: This unlikely combination of Ankamian technology and a dream ruby from the Master of Dreams should enable you to analyse your progress in the Infinite Dreams. At least in theory!
items.name: Dream Analyser

items.description: A desk, a computer, loads of imagination and a healthy dose of humour. All the ingredients needed to bring a dream to life... and to keep it alive for a full twenty years!
items.name: 20th Anniversary Dream

items.name: Primitive Statuette

items.description: Put 100 kamas in the begging bowl and give it to the disciple of Elgero in front of the Temple of Scriptures.
items.name: Elgero's Begging Bowl

items.description: You caught a quaquack! You can trade it in for a token at the Trool Fair.
items.name: Quaquack

items.description: It's your lucky day – you caught a golden quaquack! Trade it in for tokens at the Trool Fair.
items.name: Golden Quaquack

items.description: Use this fishing rod for a chance to catch a quaquack at the Trool Fair.
items.name: Fishing Rod for Quaquack

items.description: Troolokens can be traded at the Trool Fair for prizes that everyone can enjoy, from collectors to even the most pragmatic customers.
items.name: Trooloken

items.description: Gladiokens can be traded at the Trool Fair for prizes that reflect your taste for big balloon brawls.
items.name: Gladioken

items.description: You can ask Yova Etna for a new reading in 24 hours. Hopefully this time, she'll predict a glorious future for you, filled with easy victories, bulging coin purses and servants who live only to make you happy.
items.name: Trool Fair Horoscope

items.description: Use this ticket to take part in the Gladiatrool.

items.description: This token is proof of your unwavering loyalty. Bring it to Loya Loken in Astrub at [5,-17], in Brakmar at [-29,38] or Bonta at [-35,-60] to trade it for rewards.
items.name: Loyaloken

items.description:
This bag contains 50 troolokens.

items.description: New adventures, surprising new events! And sometimes, new problems... and it isn't always your fault! So, you received these recompensokens. They can be traded in for rewards with Pauly Gees at the Amakna Castle zaap at [3,-5].
items.name: Recompensoken

items.description: This token looks remarkably like the kolossokens you earn in the Kolossium arenas, but it won't fool Glad Yator and her sharp eye. Only Peltifera will accept it.
items.name: Counterfeit Kolossoken

items.description: Those fuzzy nuts with shells as hard as wood contain a type of milk that is very popular with the creatures of Osavora, especially during the season of Birth.
items.name: Nourishing Milk

items.description: If not handled carefully, this blood that comes from seasonal nuts can cause stinging burns! During the season of the Hunt, Osavorans use it to cauterise wounds... or to inflict them.
items.name: Burning Blood

items.description: To treat insomnia, you can consume this lymph during the season of Rest, but do so in moderation: overusing it may cause you to never wake up again.
items.name: Regenerating Lymph

items.description: The dimensional reducer patented by Gizmond Quelyn is even more practical than a rikiki wand! Unfortunately, it doesn't reduce taxes, else it would have made its inventor a fortune.
items.name: Dimensional Reducer

items.description:
Developed by Corporal Gobastol, this ingenious device automatically adjusts your size based on your environment. However, you should know that it isn't an enlarger. Yeah, we know what you were thinking...
You can also activate it manually, but in that case, you'll need to use orichor to power it.
items.name: Automatic Dimensional Reducer

items.description: The device provided by Gobastol will automatically measure the Kabombz nests and record highly precise topographic readings. There's nothing for you to do. Ah, if only most of your quests were like that, then you could spend more time mucking about near the Zaap or scouring the marketplace.
items.name: Field Telekameter

items.description: This type of insulation panel, which is a critical component of a microwave compiler, can be crafted on the anvil at an outpost by a handyman with enough experience. Those who can't hammer a nail without injuring themselves will usually call on a professional like Gizmond Quelyn to help them out.
items.name: Insulation Panel

items.description: Use this switch near the thermal probe located in the largest Kabombz tower; it will disable the repulsive field so you can slip inside the device. That's right – it's not the probe that will go inside you, but the reverse. Sound better?
items.name: Flow Switch

items.description: This item allows you to call Corporal Gobastol's Krosmoglob.
items.name: Corporal Gobastol's Glob-Signal

items.description: For future reference: do not upset a Dimensional Voyager when their Krosmoglob is right next to you.
items.name: Machine Debris

items.description: After buckling under the pressure and exploding violently, the technomage has reached Externam, leaving behind a pendant engraved with a religious symbol. Was the object supposed to offer protection or spiritual comfort? Either way, her prayers went unanswered.
items.name: Religious Symbol

items.description: Hopefully, this branch will protect you better than the symbol worn by the technomage under pressure.
items.name: Coral Branch

items.description: Wielded properly, this hunting tool can stun even the toughest prey.
items.name: Rhoarim Boomerang

items.description: This hunting tool can hinder prey with a brutal temperament, using their rage against them.
items.name: Rhoarim Net

items.description: This hunting tool can hobble the fastest prey from a distance with a well-placed throw.
items.name: Rhoarim Bolas

items.description: When you were offered this mission, if you'd been told you would have to go and collect animal excrement, you would have politely declined and gone off to catch some rays in the Astrub Rocky Inlet instead.
items.name: Rabbilope Droppings

items.description:
"But what really distinguishes it from other stews is its exceptionally wild flavour, enhanced by the genuine dragon drool left to steep for at least a century.
Just be careful not to shake the pot too much, or it might explode!"

— Brenshi Forgebelly
items.name: Flaming Dragon Stew

items.description: Seeing the face on this blue api, you understand that, despite your victory, the fruit-loving goblin got you to the core.
items.name: Blue Api Core

items.description: This trap is no longer all that dangerous.
items.name: Disarmed Oddnivore Trap

items.description: Just looking at it, you wouldn't think this api came from a brutapir's trunk.
items.name: Blue Api

items.description: This document indicates that the person issuing the contract is a certain Razof. The agreed amount for the baby oddnivores is really high... But you're not that kind of person.
items.name: Poachers' Contract

items.description: To properly prepare this marinade, which is very popular in Osavora, a cook will want to do so on site, in the Rhoarim village. Twelvians who aren't very experienced in the culinary arts can always get help at the Voyagers' outpost.
items.name: Roaster Marinade

items.description: Combined with other ones like it, this mark should allow you to gain an audience with the Rhoarim leader... That is, assuming you don't insult the guard keeping watch outside the royal hut.

items.name: Lionodas Spiritual Mark

items.description: This dish gives pride of place to ingredients from the birthing season in Osavora. Now let's see if you're willing to eat the whole thing.
items.name: Oddnivore Stew With Pearly Nectar

items.description: This dish gives pride of place to ingredients from the hunting season in Osavora. Now let's see if you're willing to swallow it.

items.description: This dish gives pride of place to ingredients from the resting season in Osavora. Now let's see if you're willing to bite into it.

items.description: This piece of fur symbolises the shaman's complete trust in Osamodas's chosen one.
items.name: Sekismeth's Fur

items.description: This piece of mane symbolises the king's complete trust in Osamodas's chosen one.
items.name: Lheoden's Mane

items.description: No one can explain by what miracle such a fearsome collection of ingredients could produce an edible dish. Its altogether unsettling colour contrasts sharply with its appealing aroma. Regardless, the Bwork Chef insists that this is the dish that gave the Voyagers who sampled it the strength of one hundred men.
items.name: Forbidden Stew

items.description: One might easily imagine that an Altdemon used this bucket as a chamber pot. That's not actually true, but the blood-infused water inside is still more repulsive than your least favourite aunt. Just hold it at arm's length and don't think too much about the contents.
items.name: Putrid Altdemon Water

items.description: This blue nose hair makes you wonder what could cause such an extreme change in colour. Perhaps the noble strain of the king's blood also affects his olfactory follicles?
items.name: King Nidas's Blue Nose Hair

items.description: Alchemists claim that this is the only part of the Toxoliath that isn't toxic. It's up to you whether you prefer to believe them or your survival instinct.
items.name: Tainted Toxoliath Blood

items.description: These pills contain stimulants that are highly prized by Enutrofs and Voyagers alike, though perhaps not for the same reasons.
items.name: Blue Pills

items.description: This nucleus looks like a mass of diseased flesh and seems to still be pulsating between your fingers, causing a feeling of disgust that's awfully hard to ignore.
items.name: Swollen Protoz'orror Nucleus

items.description: Corporal Gobastol has asked you to capture a Bzzulky in the Osavannah – that's done. Now all that's left is to bring it to the outpost. Avoid walking around too much if you don't want the Kabombz to escape.
items.name: Bzzulky

items.description: A metallic powder that sticks to Rotceres' fingers.
items.name: Sticky Filings

items.description: This token is awarded to the most skilled monster slayers at the end of tournaments showcasing the bravest fighters in the World of Twelve.
items.name: Monstrous Tournoken

items.description: This token is awarded to the most skilled warriors at the end of tournaments showcasing the bravest fighters in the World of Twelve.
items.name: Warrior Tournoken

items.description: Roses that never fade? Seems hard to believe. But it doesn't really matter, because the Tanukis love ephemeral art.
items.name: Pandalan Rose of the Sands

items.description: This item doesn't look like much, just an old carpenter's cup. It's nothing to launch a crusade over, or even a new archaeological dig... Even so, archaeologists and treasure lovers seem to consider it somewhat valuable.
items.name: Archaeological Treasure

items.description: This old currency hasn't been accepted by banks or marketplaces for a long time, but it still has value to Enutrofs in the Treasure Chest.
items.name: Kamoken

items.description: Every time you contribute to your guild's progression, you earn guildokens, which may be of interest to the peddlers in your guild's Merchants' Room.
items.name: Guildoken

items.description: Your guild is grateful for the efforts you and other members have made to help the guild's progression. Go to the Merchants' Room in your guild hall to trade them in.
items.name: Guild Gratitude

items.description:
These fragments, which look like a broken Dofus, are much more than just pieces of shell...
The ochre dragon has been taking refuge inside his Dofus for many years. He dreams of a better tomorrow. One existence after another, he has left behind many memories. Perhaps you should show him the ones you've found before they disappear, lost to oblivion.
items.name: Terrakourial Memory
